figures.caption: Figure 1: (a) MMRAG is effective for local VQA where the answer appears on a page. (b) Text-only Graph-based RAG supports query-focused summarization across dispersed content. (c) Our KG4VD integrates text, figures, and layout into a unified MMKG that supports long-range VQA over documents.
Figure 11: Build-time prompt for cross-page connection before canonicalization.

Table 11: Subset-level reference-free pairwise KG4VD win-rate evaluation on DLVQA. Comp, Div, and Empo denote comprehensiveness, diversity, and empowerment, respectively. ∆ denotes Ours Win minus Ours Loss.
Table 1: Accuracy (%) on MMLongBench-Doc (2k).
Figure 5: Entity and relation counts of graphs constructed by GraphRAG, RAGAnything, MegaRAG, and KG4VD across the four DLVQA subsets.
Figure 12: Query-time prompt for selecting the query-adaptive PPR expansion mode.
Figure 13: Query-time prompt for organizing retrieved entities and relations into a preliminary answer.

Table 13: Pairwise win-rate case study on DLCV_q075. Both judges prefer KG4VD over both baselines across Comprehensiveness, Diversity, and Empowerment. Candidate answers are excerpted with [. . .]; judge explanations are quoted verbatim.
Table 7: Predefined entity-type schema used on DLVQA.

Figure 2: Overall pipeline of KG4VD. KG4VD constructs a reusable multimodal knowledge graph (MMKG) for visually rich documents and uses it to support query-time retrieval and answer generation. Numbered circles indicate the major processing steps in the pipeline.

Figure 8: Qualitative example of adaptive extraction across rounds. The top row shows annotated page images, and the bottom row shows the corresponding page graphs. Covered regions are masked in later rounds to focus extraction on unresolved components. Orange outlines indicate revised nodes or edges.

Table 14: FineSurE faithfulness case study on DLCV_q036. KG4VD is the only answer judged fully faithful by both judges. Candidate answers are excerpted with [. . .]; labels show the judge category and brief reason for flagged sentences.
Figure 4: Example reflector output used to guide the next extraction round.

Table 5: DLVQA dataset statistics across four document collections. T / V / M denotes textual-heavy, visual-heavy, and mixed questions. Question and reference-summary lengths are measured in words. Visual gold-fact ratio is the percentage of cited atomic facts grounded in visual elements such as figures, charts, diagrams, tables, photos, or maps. Page span reports the number of distinct pages touched by each QA instance’s gold supporting facts.
Table 3: DLVQA results under reference-based FineSurE (Song et al., 2024) evaluation.
Figure 14: Query-time prompt for combining the preliminary answer with retrieved page images.
Figure 9: Build-time prompt for adaptive page-level entity and relation extraction.

Figure 7: Per-page extraction-round distribution across the four DLVQA subsets. Violin plots show the round distribution, boxplots show median and IQR, and diamonds mark the mean. Textbooks and ESG reports require deeper iteration than picture books and slides.

Figure 3: Representative pages from the four DLVQA domains: world history textbook, DLCV slides, environmental reports, and picture books. These examples illustrate the diversity of layouts and modalities in DLVQA, including dense text with tables and figures, narrative text with maps, technical slides with diagrams, and image-centric picture books.
Figure 10: Build-time prompt for reflection, coverage diagnosis, masking guidance, and stop-signal prediction.

Figure 6: Add and revise operations across adaptive extraction rounds on four DLVQA subsets. Add operations dominate the first round, while later rounds recover missing evidence and refine earlier graph elements.
Table 12: Subset-level DLVQA results under reference-based FineSurE (Song et al., 2024) evaluation.
